_comment: Recorded budgets for a STOCK build of build/core/dos_core.elf. Checked by scripts/budget_gate.py; write with --update. RAISING A NUMBER HERE IS THE REVIEW -- the commit that raises it must say what grew and why. See scripts/common/budgets.py for what each one means and what the frame count is and is not.
_measured: 2026-10-14 on gw-frontend, stock flags, forced re-link. THE [gamepad] SECTION (x86_pad.c) COSTS THE GUEST ONE PAGER FRAME -- do not update past this without reading why. RAM_EMU 604399848 -> 604402736: part of it was ALREADY over before this branch (october_latest's 'checkpoint' commit left __CORE_BSS_END__ at 0x24066a98, +432 B over the recorded 0x240668E8, and ITCM at 0xF2C8, +32 B over 62120 -- that ITCM figure is not from this branch, which adds no ITCM code); the rest is x86_pad.o, 2,027 B text + 114 B bss (key names, the parser, combos and the repeat state) plus ~150 B of glue in src/main.c. Trimmed once: letters, digits and F1..F12 are computed from the keyboard rows instead of listed and the name table is one packed string (3,216 -> 2,456 B over october_latest). The implied bound goes 153 -> 152 and the measured tier-2 pool 152 -> 151 (guest_ram_pages 0x97). The SDK re-sync to retro-go-sd external_cores in the same branch moved NEITHER number. Prior note: 2026-09-02 on agent/x87, stock flags, forced re-link. THE X87 ESCAPE GROUP (x86_x87.c + the rewritten .op_esc_x87) raised BOTH numbers, and the RAM one COSTS THE GUEST A PAGER FRAME -- do not update past this without reading why. ITCM 61704 -> 62088 (+384 B): the handler folds the operand, picks the read or write trap from a per-escape store mask and calls into C; it is OP_AGNOSTIC but an agnostic handler's BODY is still assembled in both operand-size passes, so the cost is doubled. RAM_EMU 604396184 -> 604399848 (+3664 B): x86_x87.o is 2,672 B of text, 10 B data and 71 B bss, plus the libgcc int64<->double helpers the FILD m64 / FISTP m64 forms pull in; dos_core.ld puts .text AND .rodata in RAM_EMU, so code IS frames. That takes the implied frame bound 154 -> 153. Two trims were tried and measured: replacing the integer casts in x87_round_int with the 2^52 add/subtract removed __aeabi_d2lz/__floatdidf from the rounding path, and -Os on x86_x87_exec made the object 4 B LARGER and was reverted. The x87 state is a file-static, NOT a member of X86CPUState, so DTCM did not move at all. Prior note: 2026-09-02 on agent/sb-adpcm, stock flags, forced re-link. RAM raised 604395336 -> 604396184 (+848 B) by the Creative ADPCM decoder in x86_io.c: 240 B of const step/adjust tables plus ~608 B of code. THE CORE IS A FLAT BLOB IN RAM_EMU -- dos_core.ld puts .text AND .rodata there -- so there is no flash to move the tables to. Nothing entered .bss beyond 8 bytes of decoder state in the static sbp struct, ITCM did NOT move (0xF108 either side), and the frame bound stayed at 154. Prior note: 2026-09-02 on agent/opcodes-bits, stock flags, forced re-link. ITCM raised 59696 -> 61704 (+2008 B) by the 0F bit and double-shift set: BT/BTS/BTR/BTC (A3/AB/B3/BB), BSF/BSR (BC/BD) and SHLD/SHRD (A4/A5/AC/AD), ten opcodes emitted TWICE (one pass per operand size). RAM and the frame bound did NOT move -- none of it touches .bss.
